claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Not coded (excluded: talk abstract). The two-page abstract summarizes an autoencoder-plus-surrogate method for real-time TO and a grammar-constrained MDP method for truss design, and asserts computational advantages with no numbers and no named classical comparator.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not coded (excluded). No runtime or comparison is reported; the abstract says only that optimization moves offline, trading costly training for virtually instantaneous inference.

notes: Excluded under PROTOCOL §3.3 and §4, which exclude presentations and abstracts-only records; FT-TYPE is the closed-list code for type exclusions. The complete item is a talk abstract ('This talk presents two machine learning-based frameworks') with no methods detail, results or comparison. FT-DUPLICATE was considered and not applied: the abstract summarizes two published articles instead of being a version of one. Its TO part cites Garayalde, Torzoni, Bruggi & Corigliano 2024, 'Real-time topology optimization via learnable mappings', IJNME 125(15):e7502, which is pool record P00090 (arXiv 2311.08473; decision order 338), the article to code for that study. Its truss part cites Garayalde, Rosafalco, Torzoni & Corigliano 2025, ASME J. Mech. Des. 147(10):101702 (not found in the pool by title). Access on 2026-09-24: hdl.handle.net redirects to re.public.polimi.it; no bot check. Screening code was I-SPEED. Authors checked: no author named Jun Wang.
